answer: At the network summit, an agent earns a violet credential only by locking a slashable bond against one provenance key. A random signal each round selects peers to re-verify that key; any duplicate identity found forfeits its bond to the auditor. Minting ten thousand fake agents therefore needs ten thousand separate bonds, all at risk of being slashed, so an attacker's cost grows linearly with the attack size while honest agents post just one.
